pages.text: Changchunsaurus parvus was a species of small herbivorous ornitischian dinosaur from the 'middle' Cretaceous of Northeast China. Its fossilized remains come from the Quantou Formation, a very recently identified dinosaur-bearing formation, deposited along the banks of a meandering river in a hot and dry environment.

Changchunsaurus and the probably closely related Jeholosaurus seem to have belonged to a distinct group of small basal ornithopods endemic to China. Changchunsaurus had a distinctly slow growth rate for an ornitischian of its size, only reaching sexual maturity around 8 years of age, possibly due to the considerable aridity and the rarity of plants in its native environment, compared to the nearby and much richer Jehol Biota.
